title: GOOSE: New option to display float values
description:
Added to the protocol a new option to display the decimal representation
of floating-point values.

Minor fixes: Avoid the double 'return' on dissect_goose_UtcTime function
and fix the simulation BLURB to follow other fields approach.

notes.body:
I attach a capture to verify the new option. Float values in this frames are:

- -777.777
- 61850.2
- 0.31

[goose_float.pcap](/uploads/9a0f98d89ff8790e2277350d9f1f0a82/goose_float.pcap)

Hi, Does the secification elaborate on: 
FloatingPoint ::= OCTET STRING
Perhaps there is no need for a preference if this is how the encoding is specified?

Hello @AndersBroman ,

For the frame analysis I believe what is really useful is its decimal representation (as the octect string is not directly interpretable).

Do you mean showing the float decimal representation always and not based on a new protocol preference?

Thank you.
I meant if the standard describes the octet string coding in any way.

Hello @guyharris @AndersBroman ,

Thanks for your replies.

After looking at the IEC61850 standard, this encoding it is related with MMS data production and not with the standard itself.

- The Edition 1 of the standard defined FLOAT32 and FLOAT64 datatypes as:

FLOAT32 Floating-point Range of values and precision as specified by IEEE 754 single precision floating point.

FLOAT64 Floating-point Range of values and precision as specified by IEEE 754 double precision floating point. 

But there were NOT standardized data attributes using type FLOAT64. 

- The Edition 2 of the standard defined only FLOAT32 datatype (FLOAT64 was removed):

**FLOAT32 Floating-point Range of values and precision as specified by IEEE 754 single precision floating point**.

The following tissue (https://iec61850.tissue-db.com/tissue/817) talks about the encoding for floating points accepting and defining for fixed-length GOOSE Message:

- Basic Data Type Float 32
- ASN.1 Tag 0x87
- ASN.1 Len = 5
- Comment: MMS Data Production: first byte=8, remaining 4 bytes represents the floating point number in IEEE 754 single precision format.

In my experience all GOOSE implementations use this format to encode floats, and as FLOAT32 is the only floating point defined in the Edition 2 of the standard, I would suggest showing the float decimal representations for these IEEE 754 single precision floating points, and keep the octet string for any others (just in case they really exist). 

What do you think about it?
Should be `FLOAT_ENC_LENGTH`.

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/1634/diffs?diff_id=139637281&start_sha=bf4200ecff60efe4da178162ba7e1fe28818647c#bbc592e25cba58e83d31ebc290d1a9b7c49957ee_89_87)
Solved on the last commit.
Should be `FT_DOUBLE`, so we can handle numbers that require a double-precision value.

Just changing that datatype generates this error on the visualization of the sample frame:

[Expert Info (Error/Malformed): Trying to fetch a double-precision floating point number with length 4]

If finally it is found necessary to add IEEE 754 double-precision floating-point, maybe I will need to add another hf to distinguish both cases. 

For the moment this is not changed and only single-precision support is included on the last commit.

[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/1634/diffs?diff_id=139637281&start_sha=bf4200ecff60efe4da178162ba7e1fe28818647c)
I don't think this adds any value...

The point here was that all the other asn1 fields generated by the asn1 generator have the blurb assigned to the datatype. You can see some examples at packet-goose.c at line 1326: 

```
{ &hf_goose_stNum,
      { "stNum", "goose.stNum",
        FT_UINT32, BASE_DEC, NULL, 0,
        "INTEGER", HFILL }},
    { &hf_goose_sqNum,
      { "sqNum", "goose.sqNum",
        FT_UINT32, BASE_DEC, NULL, 0,
        "INTEGER", HFILL }},
    { &hf_goose_simulation,
      { "simulation", "goose.simulation",
        FT_BOOLEAN, BASE_NONE, NULL, 0,
        NULL, HFILL }},
        "BOOLEAN", HFILL }},
    { &hf_goose_ndsCom,
      { "ndsCom", "goose.ndsCom",
        FT_BOOLEAN, BASE_NONE, NULL, 0,
        "BOOLEAN", HFILL }},
```
I wanted to follow the current existing criteria. I think it also could affect the filters if you want to filter by type, but I am not really sure about this.

Please confirm me if you want me to fix this and keep the NULL value.

Hi, Replace this by 
%(DEFAULT_BODY)s
